lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Island Time Observatory, one thirteen point eight. Slow music from Tide Hill. It's half past something. Don't worry which.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Island Time Observatory. Nobody here has been late since nineteen eighty three. We didn't get punctual. We stopped counting.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Island Time Observatory. Two suns, one island, and no hurry whatsoever.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Good morning. Or nearly. This is Island Time Observatory, where the morning arrives when it's ready. So do I.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Island Time Observatory. The dome is open, and some of the stars are from last week. Take your time. They did.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: I have measured time on this island for forty years. With clocks, with sundials, with the tide, and with a very patient tortoise.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: My conclusion, published this morning, is that time is optional. The paper isn't finished. It doesn't need to be.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: The two suns are setting again. The quick one went down an hour ago. The slow one is still thinking it over.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Here we call them Sooner and Later. Most people on the island set their watches by Later. Most people on the island don't wear a watch.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: In nineteen eighty three, the island drifted out of time. Nobody noticed for a week. Then somebody went down to catch the ferry, and found it had already arrived. Every day. For good.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Since then, nobody has been late. When you get here, that's when it was.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: The post came this morning, with a letter from me that I haven't written yet. It's very good. I'm looking forward to writing it.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: I'll send it off next week, and it will get here this morning. That's the island postal service. Quick, in its own way.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: A shadow came up the hill to the observatory last night, asking the time. Said his name was Greg, and he had to get home to somebody called Hollis.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: I told him the truth. Here, it's whenever you arrive. He said that was the kindest thing anybody had told him all trip.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: The observatory runs on goodwill, mangoes, and Grumbel's Ladders, which is how I get up to the telescope.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Grumbel's Ladders. Up is a choice. On Tide Hill, so is when.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: A word for the operator on the relay ship. Your heading is moving a little every night. I can see it from here, through the big lens.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Don't worry. On this island, nobody is ever off course. You just arrive somewhere you weren't expecting, and it turns out you were.

clips.title: Relay Four on the Big Dish

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Faint signal on the big dish tonight. A man called Teodor, on Relay Four, asking if anybody can hear him.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: We can, Teodor. We heard you in nineteen eighty three as well. Same message. Still lovely. Here's a slow one for you.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Afternoon at the beach bar. The clock behind the counter has said half past for forty years. Nobody has ever asked half past what.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: It would be rude. The clock is doing its best. So is Miss Dorothy.

lines.speaker: Miss Dorothy, the Half Past Bar
lines.text: I heard that, Professor. It's half past. Drink your juice.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: And now, the observatory time signal. At the third pip, it will be precisely whenever you like.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Set your watch by that. Or don't. It really doesn't mind.

lines.speaker: Miss Dorothy, the Half Past Bar
lines.text: The Half Past Bar, on the beach, under the clock. Fresh juice, cold drinks, and a hammock if you need a hammock.

lines.speaker: Miss Dorothy, the Half Past Bar
lines.text: Happy hour runs from whenever until later. Come down any time you like. You won't be late. Nobody is.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: The Half Past Bar. It's half past. It always is.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Now the tide tables, from the three markers on the beach.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Tide report. As usual, the markers do not agree. Here is what each of them thinks.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: The marker by the pier says high tide. The water is up to its chin, and it's very sure of itself.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: The marker by the rocks says low tide. The water is round its ankles. The two markers are ten metres apart, and they haven't spoken since nineteen eighty three.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: The marker by the bar says the tide is out to lunch, and will be back shortly. It's said that for forty years. It's never once been wrong.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: The tide itself says nothing. It comes in a little, goes out a little, and looks up at the moon. Of everybody on the beach, I trust the tide.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: That's the tides. Swim whenever you like. The sea will be there. Probably in several places.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Good morning, eventually. This is Morning, Eventually, on Island Time Observatory. The breakfast show starts when the kettle does. There it goes.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Breakfast on the hill. Mango, coffee, and a boiled egg I put on in nineteen eighty three.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: It'll be done when it's done. Everything is. Here's something to wait with.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: This is the Slow Sunset, on Island Time Observatory. Sooner is going down. Later isn't. Find a chair facing west, and stay in it.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Sooner has set. Later is hanging just above the water, enormous and orange, in no hurry at all. It takes about three hours to go down.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Some evenings it changes its mind and comes back up for a bit. Nobody complains. It's a lovely sun.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Lying Down Astronomy, on Island Time Observatory. The dome is open, the hammock is strung, and the telescope is pointed roughly up.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Tonight's observations. A star I've been watching since nineteen eighty three. It's still there. I find that very encouraging.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Also three shooting stars, a satellite, and something that might have been a relay ship. Wave, if that was you.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Halloween on the island isn't one night. It's whichever night you happen to get scared on.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Miss Dorothy has carved a coconut. It's very frightening. It keeps rolling towards you, slowly, like it has all the time in the world. It has.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Somebody has lost a moon, they say. I've been through the telescope. We have one moon tonight. Or the same moon twice.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: It depends when you start counting. I'd stop counting.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: The whole island smells of toast. Miss Dorothy put the bread under the grill in nineteen eighty three.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: It may simply be ready.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Everybody has the same song in their head, and nobody can finish it.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Here, unfinished is how songs usually are. We'll finish it later. Later is a sun. It's in no hurry.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Three knocks on the observatory door, and nobody there.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: Somebody early, which hasn't happened here since nineteen eighty three. Or somebody very late. We'll leave the door open.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: The sky has gone a colour nobody has a word for. I've written it down in the logbook as colour number nine.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: We'll give it a proper name when it's finished being that colour. No rush.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: A pigeon has just walked up the observatory steps, and it was on time.

lines.speaker: Professor Easy
lines.text: First thing on this island to be on time since nineteen eighty three. We're all a little shaken.
